definition.def: To extract a substance means to obtain it from something else, for example by using industrial or chemical processes.
examples: ...the traditional method of pick and shovel to extract coal. [VERB noun]
Citric acid can be extracted from the juice of oranges, lemons, limes or grapefruit. [be VERB-ed + from]
...looking at the differences in the extracted DNA. [VERB-ed]

definition.def: If you extract something from a place, you take it out or pull it out.
examples: He extracted a small notebook from his hip pocket. [VERB noun + from]
Patterson went straight to the liquor cabinet and extracted a bottle of Scotch. [VERB noun]
She reached into the wardrobe and extracted another tracksuit. [VERB noun]

definition.def: When a dentist extracts a tooth, they remove it from the patient's mouth.
examples: A dentist may decide to extract the tooth to prevent recurrent trouble. [VERB noun]
She is to go and have a tooth extracted at 3 o'clock today. [have noun VERB-ed]

definition.def: If you say that someone extracts something, you disapprove of them because they take it for themselves to gain an advantage. [disapproval]
examples: The capitalist system extracts huge profits from arms production at the tax-payers' expense. [VERB noun from noun]
He sought to extract the maximum political advantage from the cut in interest rates. [VERB noun + from]
His development policies have extracted cash from the city centre. [VERB noun from noun]

definition.def: If you extract information or a response from someone, you get it from them with difficulty, because they are unwilling to say or do what you want.
examples: He made the mistake of trying to extract further information from our director. [VERB noun + from]
He used her cash card, and the PIN number he had extracted from her, to take £500 from cashpoints. [VERB noun from noun]

definition.def: If you extract a particular piece of information, you obtain it from a larger amount or source of information.
examples: I've simply extracted a few figures. [VERB noun]
Trade figures can be extracted from export-and-import documentation at ports. [be VERB-ed + from]
...files of data extracted from the departmental archives. [VERB-ed]

definition.def: If part of a book or text is extracted from a particular book, it is printed or published. [journalism]
examples: This material has been extracted from 'Collins Good Wood Handbook'. [be VERB-ed + from]

definition.def: An extract from a book or piece of writing is a small part of it that is printed or published separately.
examples: Read this extract from an information booklet about the work of an airline cabin crew. [+ from]

definition.def: An extract is a substance that has been obtained from something else, for example by means of a chemical or industrial process.
examples: Blend in the lemon extract, lemon peel and walnuts.
...fragrances taken from plant extracts.
